claims.text:
11. hybrid-keyword-vector-search

Target / packet: ai-hybrid-keyword-vector-search · R2. Prerequisites: ai:retrieval-top-k.

Nearest / distinct payoff: retrieval-top-k → meaning-without-the-word. Pure vector top-k uses one signal; this fuses a keyword score and vector score with explicit scale and weight assumptions.

Finite primary model: Three docs A/B/C have keyword scores [1,0,.5] and vector scores [.1,.9,.4], each declared on the same [0,1] scale. Hybrid lambdakeyword+(1-lambda)vector:lambda=.5 gives[.55,.45,.45] with A first; lambda=.2 gives[.28,.72,.42] with B first.

Countercase and mathematical boundary: Scores from incomparable unnormalized scales make this weight interpretation invalid; scaling keyword by 10 at lambda=.5 makes A win with score 5.05. Stable ties A then B then C. This is fixed linear fusion, not a theorem that hybrid always improves retrieval.

Predict and recall transfer: Predict winner after reducing lambda; recall why normalizations matter before comparing weights.

Required observable evidence: Show both input signals and combined ranking; no real corpus relevance assessment claimed.

Source obligation: Declared local finite model. Exact results require independent arithmetic reproduction; this construction supports no real-model performance or universal improvement claim. Method-source obligations remain as listed in the acquisition record below.
